subject: [Multi-group analysis] I came across non-identical findings.

messages.author: f2dc317901cb92a8
messages.subject: [Multi-group analysis] I came across non-identical findings.
parts:
Hello, it is a reposting. 

I came across non-identical findings when conducting a multi-group analysis using lavaan and Mplus. Here are the codes I employed in the analysis. Would you look into it and guide me where I need to correct to get the identical findings from lavaan and Mplus? I made a table including the codes and uploaded online here for you to check: 

You could manually copy and paste to get to there: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Od04J7v-z6OKt5F__HeD6fBvYYnn_893VwoEPZ7apnM/edit?usp=sharing

Or you could check below.
 
The R codes are: 

# a multi-group analysis unconstrained

model.non.numeric1='#regression part DEPENDENT ~ MED3 + MED2 + MED1 + INDEPENDNET 

MED3 ~ MED2

MED2 ~ MED1

MED1 ~ INDEPENDNET'

fit.sem1 <-sem(model=model.non.numeric1, data=nfscm2, meanstructure=TRUE, group="group", std.lv=TRUE, mimic="Mplus")

summary(fit.sem1, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsq=TRUE)

# a multi-group analysis constrained

model.non.numeric1.constrained='

#regression part

DEPENDENT ~ c(a1,a1)*MED3 

                        + c(b1,b1)*MED2 

                        + c(c1,c1)*MED1 

                        + c(d1,d1)*INDEPENDNET

MED3 ~ c(e1,e1)*MED2

MED2 ~ c(f1,f1)*MED1

MED1 ~ c(g1,g1)*INDEPENDNET'

 fit.sem1.constrained <-sem(model=model.non.numeric1.constrained, data=nfscm2, meanstructure=TRUE, group="group", std.lv=TRUE, mimic="Mplus")

summary(fit.sem1.constrained, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsq=TRUE)

 The Mplus codes are:

!a multi-group analysis unconstrained

grouping is group (0=low 1=high);

MODEL:

DEPENDENT on INDEPENDENT; 

DEPENDENT on MED3;

DEPENDENT on MED2;

DEPENDENT on MED1;

MED3 on MED2;

MED2 on MED1;

MED1 on INDEPENDENT;

!a multi-group analysis constrained

grouping is group (0=low 1=high);

MODEL:

DEPENDENT on INDEPENDENT (cdash); 

DEPENDENT on MED3 (g); 

DEPENDENT on MED2 (f);

DEPENDENT on MED1 (e);

MED3 on MED2 (d);

MED2 on MED1 (b);

MED1 on INDEPENDENT (a);

To calculate the diff. in chi-square values, I used anova(fit.sem1, fit.sem1.constrained) in R and CHIDIST in Excel using the results from Mplus.
